idiom_name: wrapper class with __getattr__ forwarding plus explicit control methods
implementation_notes: The per-member forwarder class is unnecessary: a wrapper that holds the service and defines __getattr__ returning getattr(self._service, name) forwards every other attribute access, while the few operations that need control are written out explicitly - the data model documents attribute access as the extension point for exactly this. Call-level policy can also be applied as decorators (functools.wraps keeps the wrapped signature metadata), and for a gRPC service the framework form is a grpc.ServerInterceptor. Delegation is idiomatic but not transparent: implicit special-method lookup bypasses __getattr__, so isinstance, len, iteration and operators behave differently on the proxy unless forwarded by hand.
pitfalls: Special methods are looked up on the type, not the instance, so the proxy is not a drop-in replacement for isinstance(), len(), iteration or with-statement use unless those dunders are forwarded explicitly.
__getattr__ must raise AttributeError for anything it cannot resolve; returning None for unknown names hides typos and breaks hasattr and getattr defaults.
The wrapper hides the service's class from static analysis; annotate the proxy against a Protocol so type checkers and IDEs still see the contract.

variants.name: gRPC Python ServerInterceptor
variants.implementation_notes: For a gRPC service the framework provides both the equivalent interface (the generated servicer) and the interception point: a grpc.ServerInterceptor receives the handler resolved by continuation and returns a handler wrapper, so authentication, deadlines, tracing and error mapping are applied around every RPC without touching the servicer. One interceptor instance serves every call, so per-call data belongs in the request/context passed to the wrapper rather than on the interceptor itself.
pitfalls: One interceptor instance serves all requests: per-call state on self is a race, so pass it through the wrapping closure instead.
continuation returns None when no handler matches the call: pass that through unchanged instead of wrapping it, or unknown methods stop failing with their expected status.
A re-wrapped handler must keep the original request/response serializers or the wire contract changes silently.
Interceptors are registered per server (server_interceptors) and per channel (interceptors): configuring one side leaves the other uncontrolled.
